16 Malicious Firefox Extensions Pose as Rabby and OKX Wallets to Steal Recovery Phrases — Should Read

Sixteen malicious Firefox extensions impersonated Rabby and OKX Wallets to steal users’ recovery phrases and private keys during wallet-import flows, exfiltrating them through attacker-controlled Cloudflare Workers. Although Mozilla removed the extensions, anyone who entered wallet credentials should treat them as compromised and move assets to a newly created wallet from a clean system.

  • Researchers identified 16 malicious Firefox extensions that impersonated Rabby Wallet or OKX Wallet and were designed to steal wallet recovery phrases and private keys.
  • The extensions intercepted secrets entered during wallet-import flows and attempted to send them to attacker-controlled Cloudflare Workers, with most contacting the *.icy-star-f45c.workers.dev domain.
  • Four extensions were Rabby Wallet clones and the remaining extensions were clones of OKX Wallet.
  • As of October 5, 2026, all identified extensions had been removed, but users who entered real recovery phrases or private keys were advised to consider them compromised and move assets to a new wallet created from a clean system.
  • The campaign was assessed as a continuation of an earlier wave, with operators changing extension names and presentation details while reusing wallet interfaces, credential-handling code, and network infrastructure.

The U.S. State Department is offering up to $10 million for information locating Zhang Yu, a Chinese national charged over alleged involvement in the China-linked HAFNIUM exploitation of Microsoft Exchange servers. Zhang remains at large, while his alleged co-conspirator Xu Zewei was extradited to the United States in 2026.

  • Zhang Yu remains at large, and the charges against him have not been tested in court.
  • A federal indictment alleges that Zhang, a director at Shanghai Firetech Information Science and Technology, worked on hacking tasks assigned by the Shanghai State Security Bureau and coordinated activity with Xu Zewei.
  • The indictment alleges intrusions targeting U.S. universities and scientists working on COVID-19 vaccines, treatments, and testing, followed by exploitation of Microsoft Exchange Server flaws in the campaign known as HAFNIUM.

item.title: Tensorlake npm Compromise Spreads Shai-Hulud Credential-Stealing Worm
item.content:encoded:

TensorLake npm SDK Compromised in ChainDrop Shai-Hulud Credential-Stealing Attack — Must Read

Tensorlake’s npm SDK version 0.5.144 was compromised with the Shai-Hulud/ChainDrop credential-stealing worm, which runs during installation via a preinstall hook and can steal secrets, establish persistence, and spread through npm. Organizations that installed it should treat affected hosts as compromised, remove persistence before revoking tokens, and rebuild systems from trusted sources.

  • Tensorlake npm SDK version 0.5.144, published on October 8, 2026, contained obfuscated malicious code associated with the ChainDrop/Shai-Hulud supply-chain campaign.
  • A preinstall script ran the malicious loader during package installation, so the code could execute without a developer importing the SDK or starting an agent.
  • The payload targeted npm and GitHub tokens, AWS and Kubernetes credentials, HashiCorp Vault, SSH keys, environment files, cryptocurrency wallets, messaging-app data, and AI development-tool configuration files.
  • The malware could exfiltrate collected secrets, establish persistence, execute attacker-supplied code, and use stolen npm publishing credentials to spread to additional packages.
  • Organizations that installed tensorlake@0.5.144 are advised to isolate affected hosts, remove the gh-token-monitor persistence mechanism before revoking tokens, rotate exposed credentials, and rebuild affected environments from trusted sources.

Technologies: package-registry, ci-cd, source-control, secrets-manager, orchestration, cloud-platform

item.content:encoded:
Window: 07 Oct 22:00 → 08 Oct 02:00 UTC (4 hours)

Ransomware recovery CEO charged over secret ransom payments — Should Read

MonsterCloud owner Zohar Pinhasi has been charged with wire-fraud offenses for allegedly secretly paying ransomware gangs for decryption keys while claiming the company used proprietary recovery technology. Prosecutors say the firm facilitated more than $8 million in ransoms and charged victims over $19 million for remediation services.

  • MonsterCloud owner Zohar Pinhasi was charged with one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and two counts of wire fraud over an alleged ransomware-decryption scheme that prosecutors say operated from June 2018 through June 2023.
  • Prosecutors allege that MonsterCloud claimed it could recover encrypted customer data using proprietary technology, but instead commonly contacted ransomware operators and paid them for decryption keys.
  • The indictment alleges that MonsterCloud charged clients substantially more than the ransoms it paid, including one case involving an approximately $8,200 payment to a ransomware gang and a roughly $150,000 charge to the victim.
  • Prosecutors say Pinhasi and co-conspirators facilitated more than $8 million in ransom payments while charging hundreds of U.S. and Canadian companies more than $19 million for recovery and remediation services.
  • Pinhasi pleaded not guilty after surrendering and was released on a $2 million bond, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office.

Vendors: monstercloud, proven-data

Evolution of Web3 in Cloud Supply Chain Attacks — May Read

Supply-chain malware is increasingly using blockchain-based Web3 mechanisms to dynamically hide and update command-and-control infrastructure while stealing cloud credentials from developer systems and CI/CD pipelines. Organizations should treat unexpected blockchain traffic from development tools as suspicious and enforce endpoint monitoring and build-pipeline integrity controls.

  • Threat actors are using blockchain-based Web3 mechanisms to dynamically resolve command-and-control endpoints instead of hard-coding domains or IP addresses in malicious software.
  • The ChainDrop npm worm infected more than 400 packages and used installation-time scripts to harvest cloud identity keys, CI/CD tokens, and short-lived OIDC federation keys.
  • The PolinRider campaign targeted multiple package ecosystems, including npm, Go modules, and Packagist, and used repository settings, web resources, and IDE workspace automation to run credential-stealing loaders.
  • The article describes an evolution from smart-contract storage through transaction input data hiding to zero-value transactions that encode an active command-and-control IP address in the recipient wallet address.
  • The article recommends behavioral monitoring for unexpected blockchain activity, process-level inspection of developer and CI/CD systems, and automated controls to detect unauthorized build configuration and package-script changes.

Technologies: package-registry, ci-cd, iam, cloud-platform, source-control

Products: npm, bun-runtime, ethereum, axios, arrayref

Vendors: palo-alto-networks, npm, bun, ethereum, rust

FBI: Ongoing FortiBleed attacks lock out FortiGate VPN admins — Must Read

The FBI warns that attackers are still using leaked FortiGate SSL VPN credentials in the FortiBleed campaign to seize administrator access, lock out defenders, and establish persistence. The access has been linked to ransomware affiliates, so affected organizations should restrict external exposure, terminate VPN sessions, reset credentials, enforce MFA, and investigate for unauthorized changes.

  • The FBI warns that FortiBleed attacks continue to target exposed Fortinet FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways, using leaked, stolen, or guessed credentials to gain access.
  • Attackers have been observed extracting authentication data from compromised devices and using distributed GPU systems with Hashcat and Hashtopolis to crack stolen password hashes offline.
  • In some incidents, threat actors create administrator accounts and delete existing administrator accounts or change their passwords, locking legitimate administrators out of their devices.
  • The FBI says the FortiBleed attack chain has been used as an initial entry point by ransomware affiliates, including groups associated with INC/Lynx and Payload ransomware.
  • The FBI recommends restricting external access, terminating active VPN sessions, enforcing MFA, reviewing logs for unauthorized activity, and using PBKDF2 for administrator password storage.

Technologies: firewall, vpn

Products: fortigate, fortigate-ssl-vpn

Vendors: fortinet

Arizona courts say hackers stole info on more than 1.3 million people — Should Read

Arizona’s court system says a phishing-led cyberattack exposed and copied decades of sensitive records affecting more than 1.3 million people, including Social Security numbers, foster-care reports, and protective-order data. Investigators say no ransomware demand has been made.

  • Arizona court officials said investigators confirmed that criminals accessed and copied backup court files in a cyberattack.
  • The breach of Arizona’s Fines/Fees and Restitution Enforcement Program exposed names, Social Security numbers, and case numbers dating back 30 years for more than 1.3 million people.
  • The hackers also accessed more than 150,000 Foster Care Review Board reports dating to 2010, including reports involving 8,000 children currently in foster care.
  • Investigators believe the incident began when a court employee clicked a malicious link in an email.
  • Arizona’s court system said the incident did not involve ransomware, and no group had claimed responsibility or made a ransom demand as of Wednesday.

Attackers Hijack .gh, .sl, and .as Registries to Obtain Certificates for Google Domains — Should Read

Attackers hijacked the .gh, .sl, and .as ccTLD registries to alter DNS records and obtain unauthorized TLS certificates for Google and YouTube domains. Google blocked the certificates in Chrome and worked with certificate authorities to revoke them, highlighting the risk to any domains under the affected registries.

  • Attackers compromised the .gh, .sl, and .as country-code domain registries, changed authoritative DNS records, and obtained unauthorized HTTPS certificates for Google and YouTube domains.
  • Google stated that its own systems were not breached and used Chrome CRLSets to block the unauthorized certificates, while working with certificate authorities to revoke them for broader protection.
  • Certificate Transparency logs showed at least 12 unauthorized domain-validated certificates issued from September 22 through September 27 for seven Google and YouTube domains under the affected country-code domains.
  • Let’s Encrypt issued 11 of the 12 identified certificates and ZeroSSL issued one; all 12 were shown as revoked by Cert Spotter on October 7.
  • Google advised domain owners to monitor Certificate Transparency logs, publish strict CAA records, and report unrequested certificates to the issuing certificate authority.

Technologies: browser

Products: chrome, google-public-dns, crlset

Vendors: google, lets-encrypt, zerossl, google-trust-services

US posts $10 million reward for accused Chinese ‘Hafnium’ hacker — Should Read

The U.S. State Department is offering up to $10 million for information leading to the location of Zhang Yu, an alleged Chinese intelligence-linked hacker accused of helping lead the Hafnium campaign that compromised thousands of organizations and stole sensitive data.

  • The U.S. State Department is offering a reward of up to $10 million for information on the whereabouts of Zhang Yu, an accused key figure in the Hafnium hacking campaign.
  • U.S. officials allege that Zhang Yu, director of Shanghai Firetech Information Science and Technology, worked for the Chinese government to help breach thousands of computers and steal documents and emails.
  • Prosecutors allege Zhang and Xu Zewei conducted computer intrusions from February 2020 through June 2021, including the Hafnium campaign that compromised thousands of computers worldwide.
  • Xu Zewei was arrested in Italy in July 2025 and extradited to the United States in April, while Zhang remains at large.
  • The FBI said the Hafnium campaign targeted more than 60,000 U.S. entities and successfully victimized more than 12,700 of them.

$11 million plan for psychological support at Cyber Command gets fresh boost from lawmakers — May Read

Bipartisan lawmakers are urging Congress to fund Cyber Command’s $11 million request for sustained psychological and performance support after several summer suicides at Fort Meade. The program would aim to reduce burnout among personnel conducting high-tempo cyber operations.

  • Bipartisan groups of federal lawmakers urged congressional appropriators to fund an $11 million High Performance Team Training program for U.S. Cyber Command.
  • The funding push follows several suicide deaths during the summer at Cyber Command and the National Security Agency, which share a campus and resources at Fort Meade, Maryland.
  • Cyber Command listed the $11 million program as its second unfunded priority, saying it would provide cognitive, psychological, physical, and spiritual support for personnel conducting high-tempo cyber operations.
  • The House approved the request in its fiscal 2027 defense spending bill, while the Senate did not advance its draft.
  • Lawmakers said Cyber Command personnel can be effectively deployed in place for two- or three-year assignments without the clear endpoints, recovery periods, or unit reconstitution cycles associated with conventional deployments.

Least Privilege for AI Agents: A Practical Guide for Security Leaders — Optional

AI agents should receive unique identities and only task-specific, time-limited access to the data and tools they need, rather than inheriting broad user or shared service-account permissions. Effective least privilege also requires runtime monitoring and human approval for high-impact actions such as data exports, permission changes, and deletions.

  • Least privilege for AI agents means giving each agent its own identity and only the data, tools, and permissions needed for a specific task, with access expiring when the task ends.
  • Traditional access controls can fail for AI agents because agents may inherit broad user permissions, use shared service accounts, and act independently at machine speed.
  • OWASP identifies excessive functionality, excessive permissions, and excessive autonomy as root causes of excessive agency in AI systems.
  • Organizations should enforce access controls at runtime, compare an agent's requested task with the data and actions it attempts to use, and require human approval for high-impact actions.
  • The article recommends discovering all approved and unsanctioned agents, mapping the data each can access, removing stale permissions, and testing whether an agent's access can be quickly revoked.

Technologies: iam, api-gateway

Products: varonis-atlas, varonis-ai-gateway, varonis-data-security-platform, copilot-enterprise, claude

item.content:encoded:
Window: 07 Oct 14:00 → 07 Oct 18:00 UTC (4 hours)

DarkSword/Coruna Open Directory Finding Report — Must Read

Censys researchers found live open directories exposing the DarkSword/Coruna iOS exploit-and-wallet-theft platform, including C2 infrastructure, victim telemetry, 18 wallet-stealing modules, and evidence of a Chinese-speaking exploitation-as-a-service operator. The operators are developing but have not deployed an iOS 26 JavaScriptCore exploit chain.

  • Five publicly accessible directories exposed DarkSword/Coruna deployment material, including a distribution bundle, live beacon telemetry, an analysis workspace, a staging host, and a full C2 platform.
  • The exposed platform includes 18 modules targeting cryptocurrency wallet apps and can search photos and Notes for checksum-valid BIP39 recovery phrases.
  • A beacon on 166.88.95[.]90 recorded two Chinese iOS devices polling a watering-hole page every three seconds for hours on September 6, 2026.
  • A production-server capture contained metadata for 11 victim recovery phrases, 179 device loot directories, and a 75-account agent and reseller roster.
  • The operator is developing an iOS 26 chain involving CVE-2026-31001, but the companion kernel-privilege and sandbox-escape stages are placeholders and the chain is not deployed.

Technologies: mobile-os, browser, cloud-platform

Products: apple-ios, webkit, javascriptcore, darksword, coruna

Vendors: apple, google, cloudflare, censys

SonicWall Patches CVSS 10.0 Pre-Authentication SSRF Flaw in SMA1000 Appliances — Should Read

SonicWall released hotfixes for four SMA1000 flaws, including CVE-2026-102255, a critical CVSS 10.0 pre-authentication SSRF bug in the WorkPlace portal that could expose internal appliance functions. Organizations using affected SMA1000 6210, 7210, or 8200v versions should install the updated hotfixes immediately; SonicWall says it has no evidence of exploitation.

  • SonicWall released hotfixes for four flaws affecting SMA1000 6210, 7210, and 8200v appliances.
  • CVE-2026-102255 is a CVSS 10.0 pre-authentication server-side request forgery flaw in the SMA1000 WorkPlace portal that could allow unauthorized access to internal functionality.
  • Affected platform-hotfix releases are 12.4.3-03526 and earlier and 12.5.0-02952 and earlier; fixed versions are 12.4.3-03670 or later and 12.5.0-03082 or later.
  • The other three flaws require login and include an OS command injection issue, a Zip Slip issue that could lead to remote code execution, and stored cross-site scripting in the Appliance Management Console.
  • SonicWall said it has no evidence that any of these four newly disclosed flaws is being exploited.

Technologies: remote-access

Products: sma1000, workplace, appliance-management-console

Vendors: sonicwall, anthropic, digitalcanion, trend-micro

Unpatched Critical LMCache Flaw Lets Unauthenticated Attackers Run Code Remotely — Should Read

LMCache versions 0.3.9 through 0.5.5 contain an unpatched critical flaw that lets unauthenticated attackers remotely execute code by sending malicious pickle data to an exposed multiprocess ZeroMQ server. Operators should keep the service bound to localhost or a tightly trusted network, as no fixed release is available.

  • LMCache versions 0.3.9 through 0.5.5, as well as 0.5.6 release candidates and the development branch, are affected by CVE-2026-105192, and no patched release is available.
  • The flaw allows unauthenticated remote code execution when an LMCache multiprocess server is bound to a routable address, because it decodes untrusted ZeroMQ message data with Python pickle.
  • LMCache multiprocess servers listen only on the local machine by default, but the project's Kubernetes example binds the service to all network interfaces.
  • JFrog rated the issue 9.8 out of 10 and reported that official LMCache container images run the LMCache process as root.
  • Operators are advised to avoid assigning the multiprocess server a routable address and to restrict access to localhost or a trusted cluster network until a fix is released.

Technologies: message-queue, container-platform, orchestration

Products: lmcache, vllm, zeromq, kubernetes

Vendors: jfrog, lmcache, vllm-project

16 Malicious Firefox Extensions Steal Cryptocurrency Wallet Credentials — Should Read

Researchers identified 16 malicious Firefox extensions impersonating Rabby and OKX-style crypto wallets that steal recovery phrases and private keys, then exfiltrate them to attacker-controlled Cloudflare Workers. Mozilla has removed the extensions; anyone who entered credentials into an affected extension should immediately migrate assets to a newly created wallet from a clean device.

  • Socket Threat Research identified 16 malicious Firefox extensions that impersonated cryptocurrency wallet tools and attempted to steal wallet recovery phrases and private keys.
  • Four extensions were Rabby Wallet clones branded as “Raabby WaIIet,” while twelve used an OKX-like wallet interface titled “Portal WALLET.”
  • The functioning extensions sent captured wallet secrets to attacker-controlled Cloudflare Workers, with the Rabby clones placing raw secrets in GET request URLs and OKX-style clones sending them in POST data.
  • Mozilla had unpublished the malicious extensions as of October 5, but users who entered real recovery phrases or private keys are advised to create a new wallet from a clean environment and move assets immediately.
  • One listed extension, sipoo-grozza@browserweb.com version 2.1, contained credential-stealing code but was nonfunctional because its background script was not loaded and its message handling did not match the frontend.

Technologies: browser, cloud-platform

Products: firefox, rabby-wallet, okx-wallet, cloudflare-workers

Vendors: mozilla, rabby, okx, cloudflare, socket

PoeLLM malware infects exposed AI servers in cryptomining attacks — Should Read

PoeLLM cryptomining malware has compromised more than 3,400 exposed AI and developer-service servers, using infected hosts to scan for and exploit additional targets. It hides its command-and-control address in a GitHub-hosted poem and targets services including LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg, and Gitea.

  • PoeLLM is a cryptomining malware campaign that has compromised more than 3,400 servers, with as many as 800 infected systems active in a single day.
  • The campaign targets exposed services including LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg, and Gitea, and it has affected systems in the United States and Western Europe.
  • PoeLLM retrieves words from a poem stored in a GitHub-hosted file and converts them into the address of its command-and-control server.
  • The malware includes remote shell access, XMRig and Iron cryptocurrency miners, web scanning, and exploit-deployment capabilities.
  • Compromised servers scan ports 3000 and 4000 to find additional targets and attempt to exploit CVE-2026-42271 in LiteLLM.

Technologies: api-gateway, source-control

Products: litellm, ollama, gotenberg, gitea, ivanti-sentry, xmrig, iron

Vendors: lumen, github, ivanti, kryptex

Eight Malicious npm Packages Downloaded 40,767 Times Deliver Overlord RAT and Stealer — Should Read

The MALFEX npm supply-chain campaign distributed eight malicious packages downloaded over 40,000 times, using postinstall scripts to infect Windows systems with the Overlord RAT, a Node.js information stealer, or additional payload downloaders. Three packages remain live, with function-flag accounting for most downloads.

  • CloudSEK and Checkmarx identified the MALFEX campaign as a long-running npm supply-chain operation that has published 12 packages since August 2023, eight of which were flagged as malicious.
  • The eight identified malicious packages were downloaded 40,767 times in total, with function-flag accounting for 37,419 downloads.
  • The packages use installation-time scripts to infect Windows systems through Overlord RAT loaders, the movinlike Node.js stealer, or payload downloaders.
  • Three packages—function-flag, function-color, and cdn-img-fetch—were still live at the time of reporting.
  • The movinlike stealer targets Discord, web browsers, Telegram, and cryptocurrency wallets.

Technologies: package-registry, cloud-platform

Products: npm, node-js, overlord, solana

Vendors: github, nodejs, solana

Microsoft Outlook to block MSIX attachments starting November — Should Read

Microsoft will block .msix and .msixbundle email attachments by default in Outlook on the web and the new Outlook for Windows starting in early November, citing security risks. Exchange Online administrators can override the block through OWA mailbox policy allow lists if these installer packages are required.

  • Microsoft will add .msix and .msixbundle files to Outlook's default blocked attachment list for Outlook on the web and the new Outlook for Windows.
  • The change is scheduled to begin rolling out to Exchange Online users in early November and is expected to reach general availability by mid-November.
  • Once the policy is updated, users will not be able to send, receive, open, or download .msix or .msixbundle attachments in the affected Outlook clients.
  • Administrators can allow these file types when needed by adding them to the AllowedFileTypes setting in users' OWA mailbox policies.
  • Microsoft said the update is intended to strengthen protection against potentially unsafe attachments and that most organizations are unlikely to be affected because the file types are infrequently used.

Technologies: email-security

Products: outlook-on-the-web, new-outlook-for-windows, exchange-online

Vendors: microsoft

Oklahoma judge’s Flock ruling shows the power of Supreme Court’s digital evidence decision — Should Read

An Oklahoma federal judge suppressed evidence obtained after police used Flock license-plate-reader data to reconstruct a driver’s month-long travel history without a warrant, finding the search unconstitutional. The ruling, influenced by the Supreme Court’s Chatrie decision, could encourage broader challenges to warrantless retrospective ALPR tracking.

  • An Oklahoma federal judge ruled that a sheriff’s deputy conducted an unconstitutional warrantless search by using Flock license-plate-reader data to review Melisa Kyle’s vehicle movements over a month.
  • The deputy found 50 sightings of Kyle’s car in multiple states, then used that information to question her and search her vehicle, where methamphetamine was found.
  • Judge Sara Hill suppressed the resulting evidence and described the use of searchable historical license-plate records as persistent, dragnet-style surveillance.
  • Hill repeatedly cited the Supreme Court’s June Chatrie decision, which found Fourth Amendment limits on police searches of historical cellphone location data held by third-party companies.
  • The Oklahoma ruling is not binding precedent, but legal experts said it is among the first federal decisions to hold that some historical ALPR database searches require a warrant.

Products: flock-alpr

Vendors: flock-safety

Cyber experts call on CISA to create mandatory federal OT rules — Optional

The Operational Technology Cybersecurity Coalition is urging CISA to issue a binding directive requiring federal agencies to inventory, secure, and assign ownership of operational technology systems. The proposal follows evidence that many agencies have not met OT inventory requirements and remain exposed through issues such as internet-connected devices, default passwords, and weak network segmentation.

  • The Operational Technology Cybersecurity Coalition urged CISA to issue a binding operational directive establishing baseline cybersecurity requirements for operational technology owned by federal agencies.
  • The coalition cited attacks on hundreds of water systems in at least 12 U.S. states and said affected devices were often internet-connected, used default or no passwords, or were not separated from other networks.
  • A government watchdog found that only 7 of 22 civilian agencies it reviewed had fully met White House requirements to inventory networked operational technology and Internet of Things devices by the September 2024 deadline.
  • The proposed directive would require agencies to designate a senior official or unified office responsible for operational-technology inventory, configuration standards, and incident preparation.
  • The proposed baseline includes visibility of operational-technology assets, network separation, controlled remote access, configuration standards, incident preparedness, and verified backup and recovery.

Building an evidence-grounded agentic security operations harness on Cloudflare — Optional

  • Cyera discovered 20 malicious PostgreSQL extensions linked to the Tor2Mine cryptomining group: 16 targeting Windows and four targeting Linux.
  • The extensions load downloaders that retrieve XMRigCC cryptocurrency miners, and the Windows and Linux samples share three command-and-control domains.
  • The Linux extensions run when unloaded, extract and execute an embedded payload, copy themselves near the PostgreSQL configuration file, and add themselves to PostgreSQL preload settings for persistence.

CERT-UA reports that more than 100 compromised websites are using fake Cloudflare verification pages and ClickFix prompts to trick Windows users into installing LunexStealer. The campaign, attributed to UAC-0277, uses blockchain-hosted configuration and can deploy a malicious browser extension capable of stealing credentials, browser data, and files.

  • LunexStealer can install the LUNARAXE browser extension, which masquerades as Microsoft Office Word Editor and can steal cookies, browsing history, and credentials entered into web forms.

Ninja Forms plugin flaw exploited to hack WordPress sites — Must Read

Attackers are actively exploiting stored XSS flaws in outdated Ninja Forms and WPC Product Bundles for WooCommerce plugins to install backdoors and create hidden WordPress administrator accounts. Administrators should update to Ninja Forms 3.15.4+ and WPC Product Bundles 8.6.7+ and investigate existing sites for compromise, since patching alone does not remove persistence.

  • Attackers are exploiting stored cross-site scripting flaws in Ninja Forms versions 3.15.3 and earlier and WPC Product Bundles for WooCommerce versions 8.6.6 and earlier.
  • The attacks place malicious JavaScript in WooCommerce order data or Ninja Forms submissions, which runs when a logged-in WordPress administrator views the content.
  • The script installs a malicious plugin posing as “WP Smart Thumbnails” and creates administrator accounts, including one hidden from the WordPress dashboard’s user list.
  • The infection provides multiple ways to regain access, including a secret login URL and an unauthenticated file manager, and some persistence remains even if the malicious plugin is removed.
  • Administrators should update to Ninja Forms 3.15.4 or later and WPC Product Bundles for WooCommerce 8.6.7 or later, while checking for compromise because updates do not remove existing infections.

Linux Backdoors Impersonate Email Security Tools to Evade Detection in Korea and Taiwan — Should Read

Rapid7 uncovered Linux backdoors targeting telecom and edge appliances in South Korea and Taiwan that masquerade as local email-security tools and use covert BPF- and SMTP-based communications. The malware, including BPFDoor, Rekoobe, and the newly identified AVERAT, enables remote shell access, file transfer, proxying, and persistence while evading conventional network detection.

  • Rapid7 identified Linux backdoors targeting telecom and network appliances in South Korea and Taiwan that impersonate local email-security products and legitimate-looking processes.
  • The activity includes a new BPFDoor variant and a BPF Rekoobe build against South Korean targets, plus a previously unreported Linux implant named AVERAT deployed against Taiwanese ShareTech appliances.
  • BPFDoor uses Berkeley Packet Filter functionality to inspect incoming traffic and activates only after detecting a magic packet, with some operators wrapping triggers in HTTPS POST requests to evade network inspection.
  • AVERAT uses SMTP for command-and-control, periodically contacts mx.zxopfds[.]com over TCP port 25, and supports file transfers, process control, interactive shells, proxying, rebooting, and loading additional modules.
  • Rapid7 recommended that organizations review unexpected raw packet sockets and BPF filters, audit outbound TCP port 25 connections from non-mail processes, look for processes masquerading as common daemons, and restrict management access to edge appliances.
